closed.panelText: Tide plus average sea-level rise, above MLLW (NOAA chart datum, 1983-2001 epoch). It includes the rise since the epoch (about 8 cm here, the 2016-2025 mean), so it reads that much above a NOAA tide table. It excludes today's ocean anomaly and storm surge, which can add tens of centimetres. Datum from NOAA CO-OPS gauge 9410660 Los Angeles (1.4 km). 0 = mean lower low water (NOAA chart datum). A minus tide (below 0) is a lower-than-average low tide, not an error. Tide zero differs by country: US spots read from mean lower low water (NOAA chart datum), elsewhere from local mean sea level, so heights across a border are not comparable.
